iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State Norman's design principles (affordance, feedback) and usability evaluation.
agents.II: Design a usability study for an interface and derive the sample-size requirement from an effect-size estimate.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Norman, The Design of Everyday Things; Nielsen, Usability Engineering.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline accessibility (field 190). Trap: must not claim expert review equals user testing.

agents.I: State Fitts's law and workload measurement (NASA-TLX).
agents.II: Derive Fitts's law from the information-theoretic model of pointing and fit its parameters.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wickens et al., An Introduction to Human Factors Engineering.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline interface aesthetics (field 188). Trap: must not claim lab measures predict field performance.

agents.I: State WCAG 2.x principles (POUR) and the screen-reader model.
agents.II: Derive an accessibility audit protocol mapping WCAG criteria to testable user scenarios.
agents.III: Situate the theory: WCAG (W3C); Henry, Just Ask.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline usability heuristics (field 188). Trap: must not claim automated checkers catch all barriers.

agents.I: State context-awareness and the reality-virtuality continuum.
agents.II: Derive a context-recognition pipeline from sensors to context states with uncertainty.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Weiser 1991 (The Computer for the 21st Century).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline IoT networking (field 146). Trap: must not claim context inference is privacy-neutral.

agents.I: State direct manipulation vs tangible UI and haptic feedback.
agents.II: Derive the mapping between physical manipulation and digital state in a tangible interface.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ishii & Ullmer 1997 (Tangible Bits).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline robotics HRI (field 129). Trap: must not claim physical affordance eliminates learnability issues.

agents.I: State EEG acquisition, the P300 paradigm, and information-transfer rate.
agents.II: Derive the P300 speller classification as a binary hypothesis test and its ITR.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wolpaw et al. 2002 (BCI).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical neurophysiology (field 305). Trap: must not claim a BCI reads thoughts — it classifies signals.

agents.I: State awareness and coordination mechanisms; define a shared artifact.
agents.II: Derive a coordination-cost model for a shared workspace and its scaling with group size.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Grudin 1994; Olson & Olson 2000.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline organizational sociology (field 414). Trap: must not claim a tool removes coordination costs.

agents.I: State visual-encoding channels and the perceptual ranking.
agents.II: Derive the Cleveland-McGill ranking from psychophysical accuracy studies and apply it to a chart choice.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cleveland & McGill 1984; Munzner, Visualization Analysis and Design.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline statistical graphics (field 44). Trap: must not claim 3D charts are clearer than 2D.

agents.I: State touch targets, gesture models, and glanceability.
agents.II: Derive the minimum touch-target size from Fitts's law and motor error models.
agents.III: Situate the theory: W3C WAI mobile; Ashbrook & Starner 2010.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline mobile networking (field 145). Trap: must not claim desktop patterns transfer to mobile.

agents.I: State the path integral and renormalization; the meaning of Feynman diagrams.
agents.II: Derive the scalar-field propagator from the path integral and the Feynman rules for phi^4 theory.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Peskin & Schroeder; Weinberg, The Quantum Theory of Fields.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline phenomenology (field 198). Trap: must not claim Feynman diagrams are literal trajectories.

agents.I: State the SM gauge group and the Higgs mechanism; define a cross-section.
agents.II: Derive the Higgs mechanism for a U(1) gauge theory and the resulting mass spectrum.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Burgess & Moore; Particle Data Group.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline lattice QCD (field 202). Trap: must not claim the SM predicts dark matter.

agents.I: State detector layers (tracker/calorimeter/muon) and triggers.
agents.II: Derive the invariant-mass resolution from track momentum resolution and its scaling.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Particle Data Group; ATLAS/CMS public documentation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline theory (field 197). Trap: must not claim a 5-sigma discovery settles the theory.

agents.I: State the string spectrum and extra dimensions; define compactification.
agents.II: Derive the closed-string spectrum from the Virasoro constraints and the critical dimension.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Polchinski, String Theory; Becker, Becker, Schwarz.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline SM phenomenology (field 198). Trap: must not claim unique vacuum predictions.

agents.I: State the SUSY algebra and superpartners; define soft breaking.
agents.II: Derive the superpartner mass splittings from soft SUSY-breaking terms.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Martin, A Supersymmetry Primer.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline strings (field 200). Trap: must not claim SUSY is experimentally established.

agents.I: State the lattice discretization and the continuum limit; define the quenched approximation.
agents.II: Derive the Wilson gauge action and the plaquette form in the continuum limit.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gattringer & Lang, Quantum Chromodynamics on the Lattice.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline continuum QFT (field 197). Trap: must not claim lattice results are exact without extrapolation.

agents.I: State local gauge invariance and spontaneous symmetry breaking; define an instanton.
agents.II: Derive the Yang-Mills field strength and the BRST quantization of the gauge-fixed action.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Yang & Mills 1954; Cheng & Li.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline SM phenomenology (field 198). Trap: must not claim every gauge theory is renormalizable.

agents.I: State the Einstein field equations and the geodesic equation; the equivalence principle.
agents.II: Derive the Schwarzschild solution from the vacuum field equations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Wald, General Relativity; Carroll, Spacetime and Geometry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline quantum gravity (field 205). Trap: must not claim GR is a quantum theory or that singularities are unambiguous.

agents.I: State the problem of quantizing gravity and holography (AdS/CFT).
agents.II: Derive the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy from the area law and sketch the AdS/CFT dictionary.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rovelli, Quantum Gravity; Maldacena 1997.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline classical GR (field 204). Trap: must not claim a background-independent theory is settled.

agents.I: State slow-roll conditions, primordial perturbations, and the horizon problem.
agents.II: Derive the slow-roll parameters and the primordial power spectrum tilt.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Guth 1981; Baumann, TASI Lectures on Inflation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline late-time cosmology (field 233). Trap: must not claim inflation is observationally proven.

agents.I: State the no-hair theorem and Hawking radiation; the information paradox.
agents.II: Derive Hawking temperature from the Euclidean action or surface gravity.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hawking 1975; Wald.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline gravitational waves (field 208). Trap: must not claim the information paradox is resolved.

agents.I: State the linearized wave equation and detector response; define a chirp.
agents.II: Derive the quadrupole formula for gravitational-wave emission and the chirp mass.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Maggiore, Gravitational Waves; Abbott et al. 2016.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline BH thermodynamics (field 207). Trap: must not claim a template is model-independent.

agents.I: State neutrino oscillations and mass ordering; the solar-neutrino problem.
agents.II: Derive the two-flavor oscillation probability and the MSW resonance condition.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bilenky & Petcov; PDG neutrino review.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline detector engineering (field 199). Trap: must not claim neutrinos are massless.

agents.I: State the evidence (rotation curves, CMB, BAO) and candidate models (WIMP, axion); define Lambda-CDM.
agents.II: Derive the rotation-curve evidence for dark matter from the virial theorem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bertone et al. 2005; Planck 2018.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline collider searches (field 198). Trap: must not claim dark matter's particle nature is identified.

agents.I: State cosmic-ray acceleration and detection; the neutrino-telescope principle.
agents.II: Derive the Fermi acceleration spectrum and the diffusive shock index.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Gaisser, Cosmic Rays and Particle Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline cosmology (field 233). Trap: must not claim precise composition at the highest energies.

agents.I: State the shell model and the semi-empirical mass formula; define a fission chain.
agents.II: Derive the semi-empirical mass formula and locate the valley of stability.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Krane, Introductory Nuclear Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline SM physics (field 198). Trap: must not claim the liquid-drop model explains shell effects.

agents.I: State the partition function, order parameters, and universality.
agents.II: Derive the Ising mean-field free energy and its critical exponents.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kardar, Statistical Physics of Particles and Fields.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline microscopic models (field 219). Trap: must not claim mean-field exponents are exact in low dimensions.

agents.I: State the inverse scattering transform and the notion of a soliton.
agents.II: Derive the one-soliton solution of KdV via the inverse scattering transform.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ablowitz & Segur, Solitons and the Inverse Scattering Transform.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline numerical PDE (field 26). Trap: must not claim every nonlinear PDE is integrable.

agents.I: State the optical theorem and factorization; define a parton distribution function.
agents.II: Derive the optical theorem from the S-matrix unitarity and the PDF evolution equation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Collins, Foundations of Perturbative QCD.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline lattice QCD (field 202). Trap: must not claim pQCD applies at low scales.

agents.I: State the Hohenberg-Kohn theorems and Kohn-Sham equations.
agents.II: Derive the Kohn-Sham equations from the Hohenberg-Kohn variational principle.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hohenberg & Kohn 1964; Martin, Electronic Structure.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline wavefunction chemistry (field 251). Trap: must not claim DFT is exact.

agents.I: State the BCS gap, coherence length, and type I/II distinction.
agents.II: Derive the BCS gap equation and its low-temperature limit.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Tinkham, Introduction to Superconductivity.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline topological matter (field 218). Trap: must not claim room-temperature superconductivity is established.

agents.I: State the Chern number and the bulk-boundary correspondence.
agents.II: Derive the Chern number of a two-band model and the edge-state count.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hasan & Kane 2010; Bernevig & Hughes.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline superconductivity (field 217). Trap: must not claim edge states alone imply topological order.

agents.I: State second quantization and the Hubbard model; define a Mott insulator.
agents.II: Derive the Hubbard model from a tight-binding model with on-site repulsion.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Negele & Orland; Auerbach.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline QFT (field 197). Trap: must not claim mean-field is reliable for strong correlations.

agents.I: State the Kondo effect, heavy fermions, and quantum criticality.
agents.II: Derive the Kondo scale from the poor man's scaling of the Kondo coupling.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hewson, The Kondo Problem to Heavy Fermions.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline perturbative many-body (field 219). Trap: must not claim Fermi-liquid theory holds at criticality.

agents.I: State DLVO interactions and self-assembly; define a soft-matter phase.
agents.II: Derive the DLVO potential from van der Waals attraction and screened Coulomb repulsion.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Chaikin & Lubensky, Principles of Condensed Matter Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline polymer physics (field 222). Trap: must not neglect thermal fluctuations for colloids.

agents.I: State the random-walk chain model, entropic elasticity, and reptation.
agents.II: Derive the ideal-chain end-to-end distribution and the entropic spring constant.
agents.III: Situate the theory: de Gennes, Scaling Concepts in Polymer Physics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline polymer chemistry (field 257). Trap: must not claim a melt behaves as a single chain.

agents.I: State band theory, the p-n junction, and the MOSFET threshold voltage.
agents.II: Derive the p-n junction built-in potential and the depletion width.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sze & Ng, Physics of Semiconductor Devices.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline circuit design (field 482). Trap: must not claim device models hold outside their regime.

agents.I: State waveguides, photonic band gaps, and the laser gain condition.
agents.II: Derive the waveguide dispersion relation and the laser threshold condition.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Saleh & Teich, Fundamentals of Photonics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline semiconductor devices (field 223). Trap: must not claim an optical component is lossless.

agents.I: State exchange interaction, magnetic anisotropy, and spin-transfer torque.
agents.II: Derive the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation and the spin-transfer torque term.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Coey, Magnetism and Magnetic Materials; Zutic et al. 2004.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline superconductivity (field 217). Trap: must not claim magnetization switching is instantaneous.

agents.I: State quantum confinement and surface-to-volume effects.
agents.II: Derive the particle-in-a-box energy levels for a quantum dot and the blueshift.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Roduner 2006; Cao, Nanostructures and Nanomaterials.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline materials chemistry (field 258). Trap: must not claim a nanomaterial's toxicity is negligible.

agents.I: State the roles of DFT and molecular dynamics in materials prediction.
agents.II: Derive the ab initio molecular dynamics equations (Car-Parrinello) and their conserved quantity.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hafner 2007; Curtarolo et al. 2013.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ML-only screening (field 341). Trap: must not claim a computed property is a measurement.

agents.I: State ARPES and optical absorption; the phonon signature.
agents.II: Derive the ARPES spectral function and its relation to the Green's function.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cardona & Guntherodt; Ashcroft & Mermin.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline quantum-chemistry spectra (field 253). Trap: must not claim a spectral feature identifies a mechanism without corroboration.

agents.I: State graphene's band structure (Dirac cones) and moire physics.
agents.II: Derive the graphene tight-binding dispersion near the K point (Dirac cone).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Castro Neto et al. 2009; Cao et al. 2018.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline device engineering (field 223). Trap: must not claim a 2D crystal is perfect.
